title: Calibrated Questions
description: "How" and "what" questions that make the other side solve your problem.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: A calibrated question asks how or what rather than telling. "How am I supposed to do that?" hands the problem back, forcing the other side to engage with your constraints instead of defending theirs.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Open questions invite collaboration and make the other person feel in control, while quietly steering them to work out a solution you can accept.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: "What about this doesn't work for you?"
"How can we make this work within my budget?"

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Questions beginning with how or what.
No "why", which tends to sound like an accusation.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Replace demands with open how and what questions. Stay quiet after asking, and let them answer fully.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Questions used to corner rather than to explore.
A "how" question that is really a demand.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Answer honestly; you are not obliged to solve their problem.
Notice when a question is shifting the burden onto you.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: How and what questions invite solutions.
Silence after the question is part of the tool.
Let them solve it with you.
